classification.habit: Large deciduous tree, 20–30 m tall, with a straight buttressed trunk.
classification.habitat: Deciduous forests of the plains and lower hills, up to about 900 m.
classification.distribution: Throughout India except the arid west and high Himalaya.

identification.description: Large deciduous tree whose dried ripe fruit (Vibhitaka) is used; fruit nearly spherical to ovoid, 2.5–4 cm, greyish-brown, astringent.
identification.whole_plant: Tall deciduous tree with leaves crowded at branch ends, long spikes of small foul-smelling flowers and velvety ovoid fruits.
identification.stem: Straight trunk with bluish-grey or ash-coloured bark marked by fine longitudinal cracks.
identification.leaf: Alternate, broadly elliptic to obovate leaves, 10–20 cm long, clustered at the ends of branches, with long petioles.
identification.flower: Small, greenish-yellow, offensive-smelling flowers in axillary spikes, upper flowers male and lower bisexual.
identification.fruit: Nearly spherical to ovoid drupe, 2.5–4 cm across, obscurely five-angled; fresh ripe fruit silvery-pubescent, mature dried fruit grey or greyish-brown and slightly wrinkled; rind 3–5 mm thick; taste astringent (API).
identification.seed: Single seed inside a hard stony endocarp; kernel sweet and oily (Akshamajja), traditionally described as Madakari.
identification.bark: Bluish-grey to ash-coloured bark with fine longitudinal fissures.
identification_points: Grey to greyish-brown, slightly wrinkled, velvety surface
Hard stony endocarp with one seed

therapeutics.precautions: Ruksha and Kashaya drug: use cautiously in Vata-predominant constipation and dryness, and in debility. The seed kernel (majja) is Madakari; use only the pericarp unless a formulation specifies otherwise.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy in high doses, severe debility and emaciation, and Vataja disorders with marked dryness unless combined with Snigdha drugs.

shlokas:
बिभीतकस्त्रिलिङ्गः स्यादक्षः कर्षफलस्तु सः ।
कलिद्रुमो भूतवासस्तथा कलियुगालयः ॥
बिभीतकं स्वादुपाकं कषायं कफपित्तनुत् ।
उष्णवीर्यं हिमस्पर्शं भेदनं कासनाशनम् ।
रूक्षं नेत्रहितं केश्यं कृमिवैस्वर्यनाशनम् ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The pericarp is rich in hydrolysable tannins and phenolic acids (gallic and ellagic acids), explaining its astringent taste; the kernel contains a fixed oil (API: gallic acid, tannic acid, glycosides).

modern_information.evidence_summary: The second fruit of Triphala, Bibhitaki is excellent for balancing Kapha dosha. It supports the respiratory system and purifies the blood.
recognized_uses: Constipation and eye disorders as part of Triphala
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated at usual doses; high doses may cause loose stools. Use in pregnancy only on medical advice.
